How many sulfur atoms are in 3.00 g of iron pyrite, FeS2 (M = 120.0)?

(B) 1.51 × 1022
(C) 3.01 × 1022
(D) 6.02 × 1023

LAWS: n3:Moles = Mass / Molar Mass | n4:Avogadro's Number = 6.02 × 10^23 atoms/mol
STATES: n7:Number of S atoms | n5:Moles of FeS2 | n6:Moles of S in FeS2
CONSTRAINTS: n8:FeS2 contains 2 S atoms per molecule
EDGES: n3[Moles = Mass / Molar Mass] -supports-> n5[Moles of FeS2] (Use formula to find moles) | n5[Moles of FeS2] -derived_from-> n6[Moles of S in FeS2] (Use stoichiometry of FeS2) | n8[FeS2 contains 2 S atoms per molecule] -supports-> n6[Moles of S in FeS2] (2 S atoms per FeS2 molecule) | n6[Moles of S in FeS2] -derived_from-> n7[Number of S atoms] (Convert moles of S to atoms) | n4[Avogadro's Number = 6.02 × 10^23 atoms/mol] -supports-> n7[Number of S atoms] (Use Avogadro's number) | n7[Number of S atoms] -supports-> n9[Calculate number of S atoms] (Final target calculation)
